observations.evidence: The exact S frame and both same-registration comparison crops retain three stacked blank planks, four small navy fasteners and two posts. Soft edge rolloff and shallower face transitions visibly improve on the sharp faceted source. All three planks remain distinct at logical 192×352 use size.

Honey-gold boards retain their orange/brown family; all four hardware marks remain navy. Both lower posts now read as warm brown across their length instead of the original near-black lower flats. Face centers remain calm and blank for runtime content.

Broad soft upper-to-lower shading replaces the source hard light/dark bands. Left/right treatment is balanced, top highlights stay soft, and local seams remain shallow rather than black strips. No directional ground cast shadow is visible.

The matte cartoon wood is suggested by warm tonal response and modest softness, with sufficiently restrained surface variation. The small navy fasteners stay separate from wood without oversized glossy highlights. No target grain imitation is needed at this scale.

Inspected the raw native S frame, independently reopened S frame, single-S sheet, all light/gray/dark logical-size and enlarged background panels, comparison, and registered repeated/shared-plant-tile preview. No material clipping, black patch, broken corner, coplanar noise, detached fastener, colored halo or fringe is visible. Sign consistently draws at the front of each plant tile and leaves the plant center unobstructed.

remainingDifferences: Three native planks are intentionally preserved; the imagegen target two-board construction is a documented prompt error.
Native fasteners remain smaller and less inflated than the target, preserving their source scale and role.
Wood grain and post-face variation are more restrained than the painted target; this keeps the small blank display face readable.
The lower posts remain comparatively straight and matte, with less sculpted highlight detail than the target. Their warm values and clean form meet the frozen criteria.
